title: Meteorological and Oceanographic (METOC) Services Officer (II/ III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I
raw_text:
1. MOS 6802, Meteorological and Oceanographic (METOC) Services Officer (II/
III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I

    a. Summary. Meteorological and Oceanographic (METOC) Service Officers
plan, direct, and lead METOC operations at all levels of the operating forces
and the supporting establishment. They are subject matter experts on all
aspects of the METOC discipline and the application of it within the
decision-making process. Operating force billet assignments operating force
billet assignments for this officer include marine expeditionary forces,
marine air wings, intelligence battalions, littoral anti-air battalions,
marine littoral regiment, and marine air traffic control companies within the
marine air control squadrons. Non-operating forces billet assignments for
this officer include deputy commandant for information, HQMC, director of
intelligence, deputy commandant for aviation, aviation enablers, chief of
naval operations, N2N6E, naval information warfare center pacific, marine
corps air stations, marine corps detachment Keesler AFB, marine aviation
weapons & tactics squadron one, and marine corps intelligence schools. METOC
Officers require excellent verbal and written communication skills, advanced
competency in meteorology and littoral oceanography, and comprehension of
geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) concepts.

       b.   Prerequisites

        (1) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

        (2) Security requirement: must meet sensitive compartmented
information (SCI) eligibility guidelines based on a single scope background
investigation/T5 investigation.

        (3) Marines applying for selection as 6802 warrant officer must have
MOS 6842, the journeyman METOC analyst forecaster designation and
successfully served five or more years in a 6842 billet.

        (4) LDO Program: officers applying to the MOS 6802 LDO program must
hold the 6802 MOS as CWOs, have the NMOS 6877, have a journeyman METOC
officer (JMO) designation, and achieve selection by the board to LDO.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) METOC warrant officers are required to complete the following
courses:

            (a) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4)
within 18 months of appointment.

            (b) Complete the METOC Officer Course (N469752), Marine Corps
Intelligence Schools, Dam Neck, VA after graduation from WOBC. Any 6802 who
has not completed the METOC Officer Course within two years of appointment
will be considered unqualified and subject to termination. METOC Officers
who were commissioned prior to 2022 are exempt from this requirement.




                                        1-256                        Enclosure (1)
 1139                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (2) METOC chief warrant officers are required to complete the
following courses and to be eligible for selection to LDO captain:

                (a) Joint METOC Officers Course (JS-DDGO).

                (b) Weapons and Tactics Instructor Course (M14P2A1).

    d. Duties. For a complete list of duties and tasks, refer to MCRP 2-
10B.6, MAGTF Meteorological and Oceanographic Operations and NAVMC 3500.38,
Meteorological and Oceanographic Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Atmospheric and Space Scientists 19-2021.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
